our_view.thesis_status: Compliant every quarter since close (6 of 6 quarterly tests passed), but covenant HEADROOM has compressed sharply — from ~13% at close (Q1'25: 0.7709x cushion vs a 6.00x max) to ~2% by Q2'26 (0.1038x cushion vs a 5.00x max) — because three amendments (Aug'25, Jan'26, Apr'26) have ratcheted the covenant ceiling down faster than actual leverage has improved (Net Leverage: 5.23x -> 5.21x -> 5.28x -> 5.31x -> 5.13x [as-filed, pre-restatement] -> 4.90x). TTM Covenant EBITDA itself dipped through 2025 (from $33.3M at Q1'25 to $30.9M at Q4'25) before recovering to $32.2M by Q2'26 — so the underlying operating trend is closer to stable-to-improving than the covenant math alone suggests, but the covenant ratchet has been the dominant force, not EBITDA growth. A March 2026 restatement (an omitted $492K revenue / $39K EBITDA milestone) and a Q1 2026 compliance certificate that was never formally re-issued after that correction is the underwriting's 'reporting discipline' pillar's first real test, and it did not go cleanly — this, combined with three renegotiations in 15 months, is a materially different risk profile from a clean, unamended credit.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: A fourth consecutive quarter of TTM Covenant EBITDA decline; any quarterly Net Leverage print within 0.05x of the then-current maximum; a second reporting/restatement event or a documentation gap on a re-certification; or loss/non-renewal of a top-10 customer given how thin the remaining covenant cushion now is.

This matches 'services-project' far better than asset-heavy-industrial (no plant/equipment/order-book framing) or consumer-inventory (no physical product, no inventory anywhere in the model or the pledged collateral).

facility.draw_structure: single-advance term loan ($187,274,929.89 funded at close) + undrawn revolving commitment ($62,725,070.11 at close, unchanged through the amendments except that the Third Amendment expressly preserved it from any clawback)
facility.interest_rate: NOT DISCLOSED in any executed document reviewed (Original Credit Agreement, First/Second/Third Amendments contain no reference index, margin, or cash/PIK split anywhere in their text) — a genuine drafting/extraction gap, flagged for covenant-setup and debt-service-spec, which cannot build a rate-driven interest schedule from these documents alone.
facility.security: Blanket first-priority lien on substantially all assets of the Borrower AND its parent guarantor Veyron Holdings, LLC (co-Grantor) — accounts, contract rights, deposit accounts, equipment, IP, investment property, proceeds; full, unconditional, uncapped guaranty of payment and performance from Veyron Holdings, LLC.

facility._amendments_summary: Three executed amendments have progressively TIGHTENED the Maximum Net Leverage Ratio covenant while leaving rate, amortization (0.60%/month, unchanged throughout) and maturity untouched: First Amendment (exec. 2025-08-01, eff. 2025-08-05) cut the cap 6.00x -> 5.75x and added an unquantified cloud-migration capex basket. Second Amendment (exec. 2026-01-20, eff. 2026-01-31) cut it 5.75x -> 5.25x, added an unquantified customer-data-license investment basket, and required enhanced AR-aging reporting. Third Amendment (exec. 2026-04-20, eff. 2026-04-30) cut it 5.25x -> 5.00x and preserved the undrawn revolver commitment from clawback in exchange for undefined 'revised-reporting controls'. All three are pure covenant-reset amendments with a small bundled accommodation each and explicit no-waiver-or-novation language — none is a waiver, cure, or forbearance (no waiver document exists anywhere in this deal). A fourth, UNSIGNED draft Third Amendment (dated 2026-04-01) had proposed a materially tighter 4.75x cap with several terms left open; the version actually executed 19 days later settled at a looser 5.00x — the borrower negotiated MORE headroom than the lender's own opening draft, which is the reverse of the usual pre-signing tightening pattern and worth independent follow-up (documents alone don't explain why).
facility._note: Three executed amendments in this deal (vs. zero for Talvorn and one-plus-an-expired-waiver for Selvara) is the most extensive amendment chain in this batch — see our_view for what the resulting covenant trend actually shows.

covenants.agreement_ref: Executed Credit Agreement (Veyrona 2025 Senior Secured Credit Facility) among Veyrona Decision Systems, LLC, as Borrower; Veyron Holdings, LLC, as Guarantor/co-Grantor; and Granite Harbor Direct Lending, LP, as Administrative Agent and sole Lender. Issued January 10, 2025; effective/closing January 15, 2025; matures January 15, 2030. $250,000,000 total commitment = $187,274,929.89 funded term loan + $62,725,070.11 undrawn revolver (Schedule 1.1), refinancing $179,250,000 of legacy debt at closing. As amended by three executed amendments, each of which states in identical language that 'Net Debt, Covenant EBITDA, Test Date, and other definitions remain unchanged unless expressly modified here' -- confirmed by an independent full-text read of all three amendments: none touches pricing, amortization, day count, fees, or the EBITDA/Net Debt definitions. Only the Maximum Net Leverage Ratio threshold steps down, each amendment paired with one small bundled accommodation.
transcription_notes: Per the run's request to report the full covenant history and cross-check every quarter, all six certified quarterly test dates (2025-03-31 through 2026-06-30) were transcribed from each quarter's own Compliance_Certificate_QX_20XX.pdf 'CALCULATION' section (each a one-page PDF; no page numbering beyond page 1 of 1), cross-checked against that quarter's Covenant_Calculation_QX_20XX.xlsx 'Leverage Summary' tab -- every quarter's Funded Debt, Unrestricted Cash, TTM Covenant EBITDA and Net Leverage figure tie EXACTLY between the certificate PDF and the matching workbook (Debt check / Ratio check residuals = 0.00 in every quarter's workbook).

EXCEPTION (recorded for the orchestrator, same class of issue as a prior run in this batch, different root cause): the certified-values contract's top-level 'source' field names ONE certificate file; this borrower has six distinctly-named quarterly certificates (Compliance_Certificate_Q1_2025.pdf ... Compliance_Certificate_Q2_2026.pdf). 'source' above is set to the CURRENT period's file (Q2 2026). The engine binds ONE upstream document to the certified-values file as a whole, so the archived output's automatic 'upstream' hyperlink for the five PRIOR quarters' certified figures will resolve to the Q2 2026 PDF rather than each quarter's own certificate, even though this JSON's own per-date 'section' field names the correct file for each. A person following a historical row's link should use the 'section' text, not the row's auto-resolved upstream link, to find the actual document.

Q1 2026 STALE CERTIFICATE (per covenant-spec.json step7_signoff decision 'q1_2026_stale_certificate_handling'): the value transcribed above for 2026-03-31 (5.1265x) is the AS-FILED, certified-of-record figure -- Compliance_Certificate_Q1_2026.pdf and Covenant_Calculation_Q1_2026_AS_FILED.xlsx were both signed/delivered 2026-04-12, using PRE-restatement Q1 2026 quarterly Reported EBITDA of $8,437,990.42 in the TTM build (TTM Covenant EBITDA $31,376,744.39). The March 2026 restatement (notice dated 2026-06-20; +$39,375.18 to March 2026 EBITDA, $8,437,990.42 -> $8,477,365.60) was discovered AFTER this certificate was signed. No re-signed Q1 2026 certificate or covenant-calculation workbook exists anywhere in the deal folder (confirmed: only the three original April-2026-dated files exist under Quarterly Compliance/2026 Q1/, none touched since). The CORRECTED Q1 2026 TTM Covenant EBITDA, transcribed for reference (NOT as a certified value -- nobody has certified it) from the Q2 2026 Covenant_Calculation workbook's own 'TTM Build' tab, is $31,416,119.57 (= $7,779,229.61 + $7,280,561.04 + $7,878,963.32 + $8,477,365.60 for 2025-Q2 through 2026-Q1), giving a corrected Net Leverage of 160,852,070.94 / 31,416,119.57 = 5.1197x -- comfortably under the 5.25x threshold in effect on 2026-03-31 either way. This corrected figure is intentionally NOT entered under 'values' above (it was never certified); the model side of the engine's 2026-03-31 row will independently reproduce it, because build-monitoring-model already sourced March 2026 from the restated Quarterly_Package_2026-06-25_REVISED_MARCH-MAY.xlsx, so the model's own TTM window carries the corrected EBITDA while the certified column carries the as-filed number -- both are reported side by side by design, not merged.

performance.methodology: Company-prepared/unaudited monthly financials model (read via monitor_lib). EBITDA is the model's single pinned bridge row. Normalized metrics strip config.comparability_items. Ratios are spot on latest-month flows; leverage/coverage are TTM within the current same-basis segment when >=12 such months exist. Standouts, drift, trend and the MoM bridge are objective/mechanical and confined to same-basis segments; the line read covers EVERY IS/BS leaf with rule-based flags (no statistical gating); narrative interpretation is left to synthesis.
